title: Poco officially confirms the chipsets for the Poco F9 Pro and F9 Ultra
description: We saw the Poco F9 Ultra run Geekbench 7 with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 – that is last year’s flagship chipset and it was featured on the F8 Ultra. But we don’t have to rely on leaks anymore, Poco has officially confirmed that the new Ultra will use the same Elite Gen 5 chip. The Poco F9 series will use the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 and 8 Elite Gen 5 V-series chips Meanwhile, the Poco F9 Pro will use the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 V-series. title: vivo T5 5G's key specs, design, and launch date revealed
description: vivo launched the T5 4G in May, and last week it teased the T5 5G. Today, vivo's Indian branch announced that it will unveil the T5 5G on September 2 at 12 PM local time in India. Additionally, vivo revealed the T5 5G's key specs, including the Dimensity 7500 Turbo SoC, a 1.5K 144Hz 3D curved AMOLED display, and a 7,050 mAh battery. title: iQOO Z11 goes on sale in India
description: The iQOO Z11, introduced in India last week, is now on sale via iQOO's official website, Amazon.in, vivo exclusive stores, Reliance Digital, and other select retail stores. The iQOO Z11 comes in Aurora Green and Celestial Blue colors in India, with four memory options - 6GB/128GB, 8GB/128GB, 8GB/256GB, and 12GB/256GB, priced at INR34,999, INR39,999, INR44,999, and INR49,999, respectively. title: vivo X500 Pro Max spotted on Geekbench ahead of launch
description: vivo has confirmed that its X500 series will launch in China next month. Ahead of the launch, a vivo smartphone, believed to be the X500 Pro Max, has been spotted on Geekbench. A vivo phone with the model number V2610 has been listed on the Geekbench website. The phone is equipped with a Mediatek MT6995 chipset with 8 cores and a base frequency of 3.10 GHz. The chipset features two cores clocked at 4.55GHz, three cores at 4.35GHz, and another three at 3.10GHz. It is paired with 12GB of RAM, while the device is listed as running Android 17. title: Indian Realme C100i's box outed along with its specs and launch date
description: The Realme C100i launched in some markets back in May, and now it's finally headed to India, where it will be launched on August 27. The Indian model has a different design for its camera bump as you can see from the image below, which shows its retail box. The C100i has a 6.75-inch HD+ LCD screen with a 120Hz refresh rate and 900-nit peak brightness, the Unisoc T7250 chipset at the helm, an 8MP rear camera, a 5MP front camera, and a 6,500 mAh battery with support for 15W charging. title: Galaxy S27 Ultra tipped to be nearly the same size as S26 Ultra
description: Yesterday, a leaked CAD render revealed a redesigned rear camera layout on Samsung’s upcoming Galaxy S27 Ultra. Now, the same source has shared more details about the phone’s design. According to tipster Ice Universe, the Galaxy S27 Ultra will retain the overall design of the Galaxy S26 Ultra, with the main change being the rear camera layout. The upcoming flagship is also tipped to have almost identical dimensions to its predecessor and will retain the S Pen slot on the bottom-left side. title: Samsung Galaxy A57's One UI 9 beta is now imminent
description: Back in June, Samsung started internal testing of the One UI 9 update for the Galaxy A57 released in April. Since then, we've been patiently waiting for the first public beta to arrive, and now it's closer than ever. According to a tipster over on X, Samsung has created a One UI Beta Program section for the Galaxy A57 on its Community forum. This is one of the final steps before the first public beta is released, so it's probably only a few days away now. title: Samsung led the Southeast Asia smartphone market in Q2, was the only brand growing
description: According to a new report from Counterpoint Research (CR), the Southeast Asia (SEA) smartphone market declined by 15% in the second quarter of this year (April to June), compared to the same period last year. Obviously, rising costs for smartphones are to blame. Samsung led the market with a 24% share and was the only brand to actually grow its shipments YoY, by 6%. It was followed by Xiaomi with 18% of the pie, Oppo with 17%, Transsion (the parent company of Infinix and Tecno) with 15%, and Apple with 9%. title: Sony Xperia 10 VIII review
Sony Xperia 10 VIII is official with microSD slot, few upgrades
description: Sony just announced its latest midranger – the Xperia 10 VIII (Mark 8), and it’s easily one of the most underwhelming updates in recent memory. Very little has changed compared to the outgoing Xperia 10 VII, yet Sony is now charging €599/£549 for what is essentially last year’s phone with a new coat of paint. Xperia 10 VIII gets the same 6.1-inch LTPS OLED screen as its predecessor. It’s a FHD+ panel with a 120Hz refresh rate. title: Motorola's 2027 flagships will officially support GrapheneOS
description: GrapheneOS, the modified version of Android that is devoid of Google while still running normal Android apps and adding stronger security at the same time, is now working on supporting upcoming Motorola devices. These will ship with Motorola's normal Android skin, but you will be able to switch to GrapheneOS later if you want to, thanks to cooperation between GrapheneOS and Motorola. This will apply to 2027 flagship Motorola devices, starting with a regular non-folding device, according to GrapheneOS developers who hinted at it being the successor to the Signature. title: Gemini can now troubleshoot your Pixel 11 device
description: Google is now testing a "Device help" tool for the Pixel 11 series that is powered by Gemini. It will let you have a conversation with Gemini about things you need to troubleshoot about your phone. You can find "Device help" in the "plus" menu in Gemini. It's at the bottom of the list just above Personal Intelligence. The caveat, for now, is that this seems to be a limited test and not a mass rollout. title: iPhone 18 series prices confirmed to go up due to rising memory chip cost
description: After introducing a notable price hike to its Mac and iPad lineup back in June due to an unbearable memory chip price increase, the word on the street is that this year's iPhones will follow suit. In fact, a report from earlier this month says all iPhones from the 18 series will cost $100 more than their predecessors. The most recent report on the matter, however, comes from a more reputable source, and it confirms the earlier claims from other tipsters. title: Exynos 2700 beats the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro in internal testing, insiders say
description: Internal tests of the Exynos 2700 have Samsung LSI buzzing – the chipset outperformed Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 (both of them, actually), according to anonymous insiders. The testing was pretty thorough and included CPU, GPU, NPU and power efficiency benchmarks. First, let’s clear this up – Qualcomm has officially confirmed that there will be two Elite chips in the next generation. They are tentatively being called the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro. This is separate from the non-Elite Gen 6 chip, by the way. title: Poco F9 series global launch confirmed, design and colors revealed
description: Poco has officially confirmed the global launch of its new F9 series, which will consist of the Poco F9 Pro and F9 Ultra. The company has also revealed the phones’ design and colour options, confirming earlier leaks that the phones are rebranded versions of the Redmi K100 Pro and K100 Pro Max. The Poco F9 Pro and F9 Ultra will be unveiled globally on September 1 via an online event. Apart from confirming the launch date, Poco has also showcased the F9 Ultra in a Dark Cherry colourway, and the F9 Pro in an Aurora Green shade. title: Samsung Galaxy S26 FE: what to expect
description: Samsung’s Galaxy Event August 2026 is this Thursday and will bring the new Galaxy S26 FE. Additionally, we think that Samsung will update its flagship Galaxy Tab S series with two new models. Here is what we know (and think we know) so far. New phone, new Exynos Well, new for the series – the Samsung Galaxy S26 FE will use the Exynos 2500. The S24 FE used a cut-down Exynos 2400e, while the S25 FE used the regular Exynos 2400. title: Xiaomi 18 Fold is officially coming in September with the monstrous Xring O3 chipset
description: The next foldable smartphone from Xiaomi is not going to be called Xiaomi Mix Fold 5, but Xiaomi 18 Fold. The company has officially confirmed this. The device is going to be unveiled in September. It will be the first to use Xiaomi's new Xring O3 chipset, the successor to the Xring O1 from last year. The Xring O3 managed to score 5,228,014 points in the AnTuTu V11 benchmark. That's more than any other smartphone SoC today. description: Lava has added a new device to its portfolio in India today, the Virat V1 Pro 5G. description: The Honor Play20A is a unique model in the company’s lineup, but it may also be a missed opportunity.
